name: Roy C.
subject: Before I log off for the day
body:
I wanted to let you know where things stand.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk841&source=&t=1&akid=2323%2E124072%2EeN-jIy)
| | | |
---
Hi Peter, I’m about to log off for the day, but I wanted to let you know where things stand with our new ad.
Ever since I reached out yesterday asking for your help to keep this ad on the air, my campaign has received a surge of grassroots support from people like you. I’m so grateful.
Right now, the GOP is relentless in its attacks against me – whether it’s President Trump and Stephen Miller lying about me online and on Fox News, or dark-money super PACs putting nearly $100 million (so far) behind baseless ads smearing my name.
This Senate race is going to be a fight to the finish, and whether we have the resources to compete – and to reach North Carolina voters with ads of our own – depends on _you_. **We’re just shy of what we’d hoped to raise by the end of the day today, so I’m turning to you for help.**
[**_If you believe in my campaign and understand how important it is that we reach voters with our message before the GOP does, will you chip in $5 to make sure our new ad stays live? It’s going to take all of us to flip this critical seat, so I’m hoping I can count on your support today._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/17143?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk841&amount=5&t=8&akid=2323%2E124072%2EeN-jIy)

Roy Cooper

Peter - It’s Zoe with an important message.

Tomorrow, we hit the 100-day mark to Election Day.

That's it. That's how much time we have to flip three House seats blue and stop Republicans from cementing control.

FLIP THE HOUSE BLUE

When I voted yes on Prop 50, I knew that it could be our golden ticket to taking back the House despite Trump’s best efforts to weaponize redistricting against us.

It united Democrats. It energized voters. It proved we could win and resist Trump’s authoritarian agenda.

But I’ll be frank: we’re in the fight for our lives. Republicans are pouring hundreds of millions into this upcoming election. We need resources from grassroots donors like you to compete.

While they have mega-donors and dark money, we have the people.

So it’s up to every good Democrat to step up and capitalize on the momentum Prop 50 gave us - and all it takes is $25 to make a difference.

Will you chip in $25 today to flip the House blue and protect our democracy? >>

| A Yiddish term that means guts or courage.
---
_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=2714%2E259176%2EUSHy_T) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=2714%2E259176%2EUSHy_T)_

[](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/14404?t=10?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.07.25_Luria-Split-Chutzpah_B4_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS2&amount=25&akid=2714%2E259176%2EUSHy_T) Peter, it’s Elaine Luria, Blue Amp Action said I could reach out. _Chutzpah_ — is a Yiddish term that means _guts_ or _courage._ In 1906, my great-grandfather left his home in Poland, made the long journey through Europe and across the Atlantic, and landed in Jasper, Alabama. That took some serious _chutzpah._ My great-grandfather believed so strongly in the promise of America – a place where he could be Jewish without fear, where he could forge his own path – that he left his whole world behind. That promise came true for him. He built a life, a family, and a proud community. That’s what sets America apart, Peter. Here, anyone with a little _chutzpah_ is free to be whoever they want to be, do whatever they want to do, and achieve more than they ever dreamed. In 1993, I joined the Navy to defend those freedoms. In 2018, I ran for Congress to expand them. In 2020, I won re-election to continue that work, making our nation free, safe, and prosperous. In 2022, I served on the January 6th Committee because our Constitutional freedoms were threatened. In 2026, I’m running for Congress again, because our current representative either _can’t_ or _won’t_ protect them. The fact is that Coastal Virginia is in crisis. Our community’s been hit hard by this president’s failed agenda. **It’s time for action.** Flipping Virginia’s Second District won’t be easy. Dark money groups and super PACs are watching closely, trying to see if we’re strong enough to pose a real threat. **This will be one of the toughest fights of the 2026 election cycle.** Luckily, _chutzpah_ runs in my family. I’m not afraid of a little _mishigas._ And with you behind me, I’m ready to be the unapologetic champion Virginia families need. Human trafficking has gone digital and Washington is asleep at the wheel.

# Sunday, July 26, 2026
---|---

**Whatever happened to _Reader's Digest_?** For decades, _Reader's Digest_ was everywhere. On your grandparents' coffee table. In every doctor's waiting room. Tucked into a purse or a back pocket, because the little magazine was designed to fit. At its peak in the 1970s, it reached more than 17 million U.S. subscribers and tens of millions more worldwide, making it the most widely read magazine on Earth. DeWitt Wallace dreamed up the idea while recovering from shrapnel wounds in World War I: to condense the best magazine articles into one pocket-sized digest. [He and his wife, Lila Bell Acheson,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGSozAQAF8jMigxgASBgkvIfOmF1FgarLkTkgvNmfLvt7xf2A90V_ef23ZDTpwfv_EgJ3vZMl01kQidWz1YYi2ZMe_oxUfy_yiwLxtoMK22LZgtIKf3NjbB7URAQ0Out_OkjZ7s0kQ3BBzgToMd9eynGcIYQO9hBoNTD_u9YfehaQum13oZli5MdjEBJzN42_dzr0ZNgaWc3d_CWSLt6V1edHa-HE1yUeRZ1fBLwapglUj5Lef_Kl05HwrWT4-CNXHCFn2kWnKLObSBLhZpL0wJPSlYm9OF58UpcTVWjfpxIKdvh_xozMvBVwAAAP__9rx3qA) pictured at the link, self-published the first issue in February 1922 from a basement beneath a Greenwich Village speakeasy, mailing circulars on their wedding day to drum up charter subscriptions at $3 each. It worked. By the 1950s, _Reader's Digest_ was a cultural institution, and not just for the articles. Millions of Americans grew up flipping to _[Laughter the Best Medicine,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DEP2yAUBOBfgzdbgG0wA0OrylPToUtHi8CzeQ2GyLzEyr-v0i7Zu3863d2vy3JxmDBvP9wOltayZDhrAiI4lrojxVoyurw6Tz6Cv0FAXxbJpWq5bqVagsP0WoYm2BVAQt-AFXoaueKjNk20SvEgFAwKAh-4Gp3wJqirvwYl-34QDdp3GtdSCc5Nb7owaqOCG1XvtRCTYAOHgFSO7nfBTBHW9CpPODpf9ibZSHSvrP_C5MzkfJ5nV3Ev2eVQfXxU-geZnK-l3CqT83f32CLB0VKE9itUai_vVZiByfknuABHbb_hBpU-9QcyeuKTGbU2WpvmsOF-YkpYlWYD33aH6W83-q9Dn1b-CQAA__9y_4l-)_ swapping jokes from _Life in These United States_ and [_Humor in Uniform_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1uhDAUBODTmG7R8_MfFC7S0G3alMjYj8VZgxF2Fu3tI3KFtJ9GM9J83ce7iyluj0-3kq1zHjc6S6Ja6RjLGutS8hbdNjtf_UL-SSH6PCKgvoG5oR6Di-k9yibYmQhJNGS56RRoUKZvFqsmaVAA590EnVFqmmRQXIugjZkQeBPt1QYGNQfoRd8GZXodnNLCG847ziRQiDUf7XeOW11oTu_8oqP1eW2SXWrdCxMfDAeGw3me7ew8TTk_rwDD4XHkn70wHKbD1TLHdOGeS72MA9dCSWkESIkoDcOhOWzYz5hSLNowCY_VxfS3Vv910cvibwAAAP__Txp2wA), and testing themselves with the monthly _Word Power_ vocabulary quiz. The _Reader 's Digest_ Condensed Books series, launched in 1950, became a living-room staple of its own, delivering abridged bestsellers by direct mail for nearly five decades before being renamed Select Editions in 1997. You can still [buy original sets on eBay](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykk89zmzgUx_8a-WaP9CQkdODgBHs22SSz9ma3bS6MEDKICERBgbh_fQfodNoeeqkOmvfz-z5vRvrwmD0q62xbPqnGJOHis9ZMgzMhmD4bGhuqwbdWtRelg66MfjWF1T4DDHyLxRZ4VijrrhnbFMnFGDB0YxIi4ghzHAm5qRKIhL5EhgoGLC8EAUVjJrG5aF3kMWUbm8xqWAAnGEsqd0UkJC9UxKkWhMQEMWwKG3y_q71tQ2Uu7upH0--0bzYuqULoBkT3CI4IjtM07UyurnMSwdGG-aacU8wjYBBzRI-6ahFNuwEBH1WPaMopJ5hHggEBBLz1_ayPaEoQ8ObVjOG73dsC0VQQsiVEkBi2VIDEW7wk9ZKExR5Wh-C5zwbTLO6Pk7KfsIAH1ZcmrBIswsAkSC5khIAXZrTaIJrqRTtcu9npnELAS-9LZ5zXiKYSQxzLWazzFtEUAdeq6ZQt21WXAGGURDRetyl7_9atnHFMYgaME6AIeO8GtfKsc7a_Eqlc3819kmERwTyxMb2uVLsuwOdCYDOeKrLBv_ULPvkW-A1UmfdqCeP9fNLslFbZuf58wNrXz_LL0__NC4HncD3fz9XaLcW3Nf779lRPkuXPN1V62p_vhv0THUf8ngd78y8G4qrjocodebz_rx5PcCJ3tPkkzx8Pf6WmNhd4_-fhfP8ujicyaLV_q14O-4cpm_TNpk-KbrLO2YELxHDZKOuWxxf-6MeMCXwNAAD__ydKDgY). But the digital age hit hard, and a debt-laden 2007 leveraged buyout made things worse. The company filed for bankruptcy in 2009 and again in 2013. Today, the U.S. print edition still publishes about six times a year with a circulation of around 1.6 million, a fraction of its former reach. The parent company, now called Trusted Media Brands, has pivoted to digital and streaming video. The little magazine that once outsold everything but the Bible is still around, but it's a (should we say it?) condensed digest of what it was. _Did you grow up reading Reader's Digest? For decades, Reader's Digest was everywhere. On your grandparents' coffee table. In every doctor's waiting room. Tucked into a purse or a back pocket, because the little magazine was designed to fit. At its peak in the 1970s, it reached more than 17 million U.S. subscribers and tens of millions more worldwide, making it the most widely read magazine on Earth. DeWitt Wallace dreamed up the idea while recovering from shrapnel wounds in World War I: to condense the best magazine articles into one pocket-sized digest. pictured at the link, self-published the first issue in February 1922 from a basement beneath a Greenwich Village speakeasy, mailing circulars on their wedding day to drum up charter subscriptions at $3 each. It worked. By the 1950s, Reader's Digest was a cultural institution, and not just for the articles. Millions of Americans grew up flipping to - swapping jokes from Life in These United States and , and testing themselves with the monthly Word Power vocabulary quiz. The Reader 's Digest Condensed Books series, launched in 1950, became a living-room staple of its own, delivering abridged bestsellers by direct mail for nearly five decades before being renamed Select Editions in 1997. Today, the U.S. print edition still publishes about six times a year with a circulation of around 1.6 million, a fraction of its former reach. The parent company, now called Trusted Media Brands, has pivoted to digital and streaming video. ## No Drugs in Houston Shooting Van
The crystal-like substance that FBI agents spotted in Lorenzo Salgado Araujo's work van after an ICE agent shot him fatally [tested negative for narcotics](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOgyAYhJ9Gb5hfQNQDh7146173aFB-hAShkb-1fftNm-4T7HUymZlvfi7zxYQY0vZtdtT0cHlOeJaIRHjMKdvjtpWQfL4Vyqn4nCmk7T5z4IpBz7iarQnxOcva6gXs2Nao237oQIlBQO21WkYFpmt74_qxkwOMYrRgnOukxFXxOuhXGPRctS0IKRqzghhaRCeAr90ClQS0gfLRkEfChykuPvMdj2bNex21J7qWSnxVfKr4dJ5n4_KDq8_ml6ni04uq4tNHZGFF9kfDym0pZNKKLGVib2S2I3mzXz2S2UPC-tD2eoYYQ1F9JWHbTYjvfvrfa3fNfwMAAP__DOKFMg), the Harris County District Attorney's Office confirmed Friday. Salgado Araujo's family said all along that the bags held a [homemade electrolyte mix](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O3DAMhU8jdzJoyn9TqEjjbtOmNDiSbCsriwtJtmdy-sBBbrAdARL8vvd-fcwf5IOP60_anS6vheforhxcKS7NkW061uzjxkcuHPPGXHxczxkBewmDxH625MN7biurn2AfTeV0M4wd9GpUUG16VN34WNA-qAczqq4f0NhFdYhPIAWm8vp-BgP2TQOqVTUZUGPj3KIATfcE0YKzvnCqy-aKe1FewptPl2rDexX0VspXFuqHwEngdF1XbYI3n_hf-r4SON2xBE6BDQWB080UOMFwz-29ZxkpGS7eZLnwEa30UQZOLv5hmSmsZFlSouM3Z3lx-pQnRWk4rsnlfPFOUWZ635Aqaft1-RB87gfRwrqTD_9sy_c6PjX-DQAA__8aKpKp) of granulated salt, lemon, and water that outdoor crews use in Texas heat. Their attorney, Ruby Powers, said full lab results are due Monday. Homeland Security has said the 52-year-old tried to run over an agent during a targeted enforcement operation in Magnolia Park on July 7. Men riding in the van dispute that account, saying the agents' vehicles struck them first. District Attorney Sean Teare had already said the drug question had no bearing on whether deadly force was justified. ## Paxton Wins Discord Child-Safety Order
A Collin County [judge ordered Discord](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAQRp8Gd0R4-LFdUGxDd7fd0uJnHLOLIQIS37z9ynmF2410Rkc635-v9cvGFPP9tz1Q9--trBnPlrB3rGsuoT7vLea9PFsvue2l9JjvrxUYKMomCmoNNqb3KoagHQvLOKAep1kyxWfOhl2LiYstODWPOKKSYlFykn5Wk18QnJdD1JeMTaDGkXHBb9YzPo-IG2fgpWNEMAyxl3rrO3b8tm1L7_LCevPlGJLee380wn8RMATMeZ63K-HE1pfrg4CxtUefkIC5CAGTireJgPnYCJgQmy810GY37G96oG3Pio1-OP0Xw3Uej1JtfdOY_z6z77FkAgbUQnFRGzqw1KEcqfBuoU45Tr230nsnN8vFUHV4nDGl2NREBLsfNqZPQP_Z7C8N_wMAAP__3nSY7w) to give every Texas user the same age verification and default safety settings the company already provides in the United Kingdom within 90 days. Attorney General Ken Paxton's office [sued Discord on May 22](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL8OmzAQxp8GNiNjDCSDhy5s6doRGfswpzo-ZF8gvH2VqH2Cbt_w0_fv12N-WIyYwk_7BMPvleYEZ4nADHlO5PMrFEwbvQpTKhsRYwrHrKQahByFGmZvMV6zrr1ZpL-3NZh2vPVy6G6drDfT65vXer2P0ko19Isf771upXJO28WPS43mYyZHNbSt7HTXWCe7WwuwdlK5fpGVluCRKTe8AcPbljVedEBuHD3raDbmvVTdj0pNlZrO82y-kGWmnOAKkCDb2AQ6KjV91lVqyhDBFvjIf5z4C4rfkMRu30xJFHCvDEVsWJgyOhEh2CgOdEz5EitlhykIj8VR9mLPxOBYfPOF2zD6DKnOxu8nxohlGCstw9Ni_Hbn_3v8MOpPAAAA___zC5zN) under the Deceptive Trade Practices Act, arguing the platform told parents it was safe by design while defaulting children's accounts to its weakest settings. The agreed injunction followed a two-day hearing. Under the order, messages from strangers route to a separate request inbox, sensitive content stays locked for Texas teens unless Discord confirms an adult, and adult-only spaces close to anyone not age-verified. Discord said it agreed with the attorney general's office on steps that support a safer experience for teens. The company filed 489,782 reports of suspected child exploitation to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children last year.
